# Two Emissions Rules in One Program

The program used different mechanisms for sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. The sulfur dioxide mechanism set an aggregate cap and allowed trading, with each allowance covering one ton.

The nitrogen oxides component was rate-based for certain coal-fired units. It began in 1996 and did not introduce a cap or allowance trading. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units.

Phase II began in 2000. The final 2010 cap was 8.95 million tons.
